ratio.note: Not a single constant modular ratio. The desktop jump from h2 to h1 (1.82) is far larger than the steps below it (1.22, 1.13): one large display size sits above an almost-flat cluster of subordinate sizes.

bodyCandidates.fontSize: 100% (16px at UA default; no rem/px override on body)

typography.fluidTypeEvidence: clamp() occurs exactly once in all fetched CSS and it sizes a sidebar width, not type: @media(min-width:66rem) .post__aside--left.post__aside--default{--dynamic-aside-width:clamp(13.75rem,calc(-12.122rem + 39.2vw),18.75rem)}. vw appears 3 times total (that clamp, .breakout{margin:0 calc(50% - 50vw)}, .full-size-interactive{width:100vw}). No font-size uses clamp() or vw. Type scales by discrete media-query steps.

spacing.evidence: Tallied every margin/padding/gap value in all 18 fetched CSS files. Two parallel systems. (1) An em-relative typographic rhythm on a 0.25em step (1em x66, 2em x42, 3em x33, 1.5em x23, .5em x23, .75em x19, .25em x16) — 363 weighted declarations, the larger of the two. (2) An absolute rem/px scale — 480 weighted declarations, of which 63.1% land on a 4px grid and 83.5% on a 2px grid (5px: 42.1%, 8px: 40.1%, 10px: 36.5%), which is why 4px is the inferred unit rather than 8px. Off-grid outliers with count>=5 are 30px (x29) and 60px (3.75rem, x16) — a 30px sub-rhythm tied to the 60px mobile header height — plus 15px, 35px, 50px and 1px/2px hairlines.

color.darkModeEvidence: prefers-color-scheme appears 0 times in all 18 fetched CSS files. No data-theme attribute on <html> or <body> on either page (<html lang='en'>; body classes are page/template names only). The 8 `.dark` rules in sheet-3.css are a link/underline style variant (.dark{color:#1a1a1a} on a white ground), not a dark theme. --theme-background is only ever declared as white.

layout.breakpointNote: 424 @media blocks in total. Units are mixed em/rem/px, and the same logical stop is written several ways (34em and 34rem; 66em, 65.99em and 66rem; 48em, 48rem and 768px), so the counts above are per written form. Three stops carry almost all the weight: 34em (544px), 50em (800px) and 66em (1056px). 20em (320px) is an explicit floor.

contentWidthCandidates.selectorEvidence: .max-w-mod-inline{max-width:35rem} — the narrowest named module width, the in-column reading measure
.post__content--legacy{max-width:calc(615px + 2.5rem)} then calc(615px + 5rem); .post__content--legacy .container--xs{max-width:615px} — the legacy article reading measure

layout.contentWidthNote: Two overlapping systems coexist: a Tailwind-style responsive `.container` that steps 544 -> 688 -> 736 -> 768 -> 1025 -> 1056 -> 1360 -> 1728px, and a named editorial module scale (mod-inline 560, mod-small 740, mod-regular 920, mod-medium 1160, mod-large 1300) that widths images and callouts independently of the text column. The prose measure itself is the narrow end: 560px for inline modules, 615px for legacy article content — roughly 60-70 characters at 16px Merriweather. That gap between a ~600px text column and a 1360-1728px outer container is where the whitespace comes from.

gridUsage.evidence: display:grid appears in 9 rules (.grid utility, .mega__other.grid, author lists, .post__aside--right .abstractions.insights, a 1fr/35rem/1fr image-meta track at min-width:66em, and responsive .mini-a\:grid / .l-\:grid utilities). display:flex appears in 46 rules and is the dominant layout mode; display:inline-flex is never used. Layout is flex-first with grid reserved for a few explicit multi-track cases.

Modal / lightbox — .modal shell with .modal--lightbox variant and .modal__close

behaviours.evidence: 23 srcset attributes on the home page, 33 elements. No loading="lazy" and no data-src on either page, so images are eagerly loaded at the browser-chosen density.

behaviours.evidence: Scripts comment_count.js and comment_embed.js; 21 data-disqus-identifier attributes on the home page.

behaviours.evidence: ABSENT. No dialog/combobox role, no keydown-bound palette markup, no aria-controls listbox in either page. The search overlay is a plain form, not a palette.

behaviours.name: copy button
behaviours.evidence: ABSENT. No "clipboard" or "copy-link" token in either page and no matching CSS class.

behaviours.name: scroll-driven effects
behaviours.evidence: ABSENT from static evidence. No IntersectionObserver string in the served HTML, no .is-scrolled / hide-on-scroll state class in any fetched stylesheet, no scroll-timeline or animation-timeline. The header does not change on scroll by CSS. Note: main.min.js was NOT fetched, so a JS-only scroll effect could not be ruled out.

behaviours.name: reduced-motion respect
behaviours.evidence: ABSENT. prefers-reduced-motion appears 0 times in all 18 fetched stylesheets, while transition/transform are used throughout the nav and modal states.

notes: Method: curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent, -L, --max-time 20. Both pages returned HTTP 200 on the first attempt; no bot challenge, no retries needed.

Both pages are genuinely server-rendered, not a JS shell: home.html carries 6,789 characters of visible text with 1 h1, 6 h2, 21 h3 and 33 img; biology.html carries 6,014 characters with 1 h1, 4 h2, 10 h3. Status is "fetched", not "js-rendered".

The 2.8-3.1% text-to-HTML ratio is not evidence of emptiness. It reflects 61-76 inline <svg> icons, 23 srcset attributes with many candidates each, and long Tailwind-style utility class strings on nearly every element.
All 4 linked stylesheets fetched successfully (208,235 bytes total) plus 14 inline <style> blocks (13,955 bytes of CSS). No @import in any page or stylesheet, so the CSS graph is complete.

Every value here is measured from the saved markup or CSS, or explicitly labelled inferred. Nothing is from rendering: no computed styles, no layout boxes, no actual rendered text measure, no screenshots.

Because there is no computed-style pass, cascade winners are not resolved. Where a property is declared several times (font-size on h1, background on body) the media-query context is quoted so the reader can see which declaration applies at which width.

JavaScript bundles (main.min.js, edin.js, jQuery) were deliberately NOT fetched. Every behaviour is inferred from DOM structure, state-class names in CSS, and script filenames only. Absences marked ABSENT are absences of static evidence, not proof the behaviour does not exist.
body background is never set with an explicit background-color declaration; #ffffff comes from --theme-background on body and body.custom-colors. Recorded as a candidate, not a computed value.

Raw HTML and CSS live under data/design-study/raw/quantamagazine_org/ (gitignored). No stylesheet, asset, illustration, font file or page text was copied into the repository; this JSON records measurements in our own vocabulary only.

browserPass.tool: Claude Code Browser pane (Chromium), computed styles via javascript_tool
browserPass.notes: Desktop emulated at 1440x900. Home page is an index; the reading column was measured on a dated feature article. Cookie banner declined with Reject All before the desktop pass.

pagesMeasured: https://www.quantamagazine.org/genome-duplication-is-a-radical-evolutionary-gamble-20260902/ (a dated feature article, used for the reading column)
measured.method: Chromium computed styles via javascript_tool. Desktop emulated at 1440x900 (the pane's own 'desktop' preset reports a 0x0 viewport); mobile at the 375x812 preset with a reload. Characters per line = paragraph content-box width / average glyph width of a 100-character lorem span in the paragraph's exact computed font styles. The cookie banner was declined with 'Reject All' before the desktop article measurement; nothing was accepted.

homePage.note: The home page is an index: its only paragraph over 40 characters is a 360px about-block set in the UI face, not the reading face. Reading values come from the article.

readingColumn.verticalRhythm: Paragraph margin-bottom (30px) is exactly the line-height (30px): one blank line between paragraphs, so the baseline grid survives across the whole article.
readingColumn.note: 560px at 16px serif gives 73 characters per line — the only measured site in this set that lands inside the 45-75 range. The column is narrower in pixels than every other reference here, and the widest in characters is not the widest in pixels.

contrast.note: Near-black on pure white; the only light-scheme reference measured so far.

headings.threeTypefaceRule: Noe Display (serif display) for the article title, Merriweather (serif text) for body and section headings, Pangram (sans) for labels, kickers and interface. h3 here is smaller than body text — it is a metadata label, not a third prose level.
headings.note: h2 margin-top 38.5px is 1.75 line-heights above and 19.25px (0.64) below — an asymmetric space that binds a heading to the text under it.

figcaption.lineHeightNote: Computed line-height of 0px on the figure element measured; the caption's own text node may inherit a different value, so this figure is reported as read and not interpreted.

chrome.headerHeightNote: The <header> element itself computes to zero height. Site navigation lives in a fixed full-viewport 'mega' overlay (1440x900, z-index 0) that is out of view until opened — there is no persistent visible top bar over the article.
stickyOrFixedElements: div.mega.fixed (1440x900, z 0) — the closed navigation overlay
div.cky-consent-container (1440x131, z 9999999) — the consent banner, declined
chrome.note: Nothing follows the reader down the page: no sticky header, no progress bar, no sticky share rail.

desktop.tocReason: No element 80-460px wide holding three or more in-page anchors. A Quanta feature has no in-page navigation.

search.note: A real input with a visible placeholder and an orange submit button, not a dialog trigger; no keyboard shortcut is advertised.

pageWeight.note: 0.07 text-to-HTML is the highest ratio measured in this set — the markup is mostly the article.

readingColumn.marginCaveat: The longest-paragraph match at this width reported margin-bottom 0px where desktop reported 30px. Recorded as measured; the discrepancy was not chased, so treat the 30px rhythm as confirmed for desktop only.

mobile.bodyUnchangedAtMobile: 16px/30px at both 1440px and 375px — body type does not move at all.

h1.fractionalSizeNote: 24.96px and 28.704px are non-integer, so the article title is fluid (a vw or clamp expression), not a fixed breakpoint step.

search.note: The search input still renders at 375px rather than collapsing behind the menu control.

consentBanner.note: The banner returned after the viewport switch (a new device profile, so the earlier 'Reject All' did not carry). It was not clicked again and nothing was accepted. It covers 44% of the mobile viewport height but does not change any measured box, since all values come from getBoundingClientRect on the elements themselves.

inferred.intersectionObserverNote: Not found in the 39 script sources or scanned inline text. Consistent with a page that has no scroll-linked chrome.
inferred.colorSchemeNote: No color-scheme declaration and no data-theme attribute: the light rendering is the only rendering; there is no dark mode to detect.
fontsDeclared: Merriweather 300/400/700, roman and italic (roman + italic loaded)
Pangram 100-900 (declared; the weights sampled were unloaded on the article)
inferred.classNaming: Readable BEM-ish plus utility atoms in the same string ('post__content wysiwyg p theme__anchors--', 'mega fixed fit-x z0 bg-black') — a WordPress-era authored stylesheet, not a compiled utility framework.
